accepted.title: Annulation Reaction of Vinyl/Propargyl Sulfonium Salts with Carbon Nucleophiles: Stereoselective Synthesis of Functionalized Bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane Scaffolds
accepted.abstract: Abstract Stereoselective cascade annulation reaction of vinyl/propargyl sulfonium salts with C-nucleophiles enables rapid construction of functionalized bicyclo[3.1.0]hexanes, bearing contiguous stereocenters, in good yields. This transformation proceeds via a Michael addition reaction of a C-nucleophile to a vinyl/allenyl sulfonium system, followed by an intramolecular Corey–Chaykovsky-type reaction, and consequently affords structurally complex bicyclic frameworks. This operationally simple strategy provides an efficient entry to synthetically challenging and densely functionalized carbocyclic scaffolds under mild conditions.

accepted.title: Carbene-Catalyzed Enantioselective Formal [4 + 2] Reaction for Rapid Synthesis of 1-Azaspiro[4,5]decane Derivatives
accepted.abstract: Abstract An NHC-promoted formal [4 + 2] cycloaddition reaction is developed for quick access to chiral 1-aza-spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone molecules bearing quaternary chiral carbon centers. A broad scope of β-methylenals and 5-ene pyrrolin-4-one substrates worked well in this reaction. A diversity of chiral 1-aza-spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone molecules can be afforded in generally moderate to good yields and excellent enantioselectivities. The chiral products obtained from this protocol can be transformed into multifunctional chiral spirocyclohexane pyrrolidone derivatives through simple operations.

accepted.title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Synthesis of 3-Hydroxyisoindolinones from Phthalimide Imines
accepted.abstract: Abstract We report an electrochemical method for the radical–radical coupling of alkyl iodides with phthalimide imines under mild conditions. This operationally simple electro-reductive procedure enables selective reduction of carbonyl groups, offering an efficient route to access functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones in moderate-to-excellent yields. Notably, the highly functionalized 3-hydroxyisoindolinones have shown promising bioactivity in preliminary assessments, pointing to the significant potential of this chemical scaffold for anticancer cell applications. A comparative analysis has demonstrated that the hydrazone moiety within the product structure plays an indispensable role in conferring bioactivity.

accepted.title: Electrolyte- and Catalyst-Free Electrochemical Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Diorganoyl Selenides
accepted.abstract: Abstract A facile electrocatalytic radical coupling of Katritzky salts with diselenides for the efficient synthesis of various alkyl aryl unsymmetrical selenides has been developed under mild conditions. This sustainable protocol is driven by renewable electrical energy, features a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and practical scalability. The reaction proceeds without the need for any external electrolyte, catalyst, or metal, in accordance with green chemistry principles.

accepted.title: FeBr3-Catalyzed Aromatization-C–O Bond Cleavage Process for Construction of Aryl-Substituted Prostaglandin Skeleton
accepted.abstract: Abstract Prostaglandins exhibit therapeutic potential in multiple diseases and the incorporation of aromatic rings into their side chains can often enhance their corresponding biological activities. Although more than 20 kinds of drugs are currently used in clinical practice, there are huge difficulties in the preparation of both active pharmaceutical ingredients and preparations. Prostaglandins directly substituted by aryl groups may overcome these difficulties; however, their preparation remains challenging, and only a few synthetic methods have been reported to date. Herein, we describe a novel FeBr3/ligand-catalyzed aromatization-C−O bond cleavage process that provides access to aryl-substituted prostaglandin skeletons.

accepted.title: Metal-Free Divergent Synthesis of Dithiophosphinates and Phosphine Sulfides via Photocatalytic Multicomponent Reactions
accepted.abstract: Abstract A photocatalytic multicomponent reaction has been developed for the synthesis of dithiophosphinates with exclusive anti-Markovnikov selectivity and 100% atom economy, using the easily-available Rhodamine 6G (RhB 6G) as the photocatalyst. This method enables the one-pot construction of S–C–P=S four chemical bonds from easily-available diphenylphosphine, elemental sulfur, and alkenes in THF solvent, and tolerates a variety of alkenes including mono-, di-, and even tri-substituted ones and can be easily scaled up in gram scale, showing excellent practicality. Moreover, the selective synthesis of valuable phosphine sulfides with exclusive anti-Markovnikov selectivity from identical starting materials can also be achieved by controlling the loading of elemental sulfur and conducting under neat (solvent-free) conditions.

accepted.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Cascade 5- exo-dig Annulation and Amination for Assembly of Amino-Functionalized Trisubstituted Furans
accepted.abstract: Abstract A novel route for the preparation of trisubstituted furans with an amino functional group is presented as a palladium-catalyzed cascade 5-exo-dig annulation/amination reaction of α-alkynyl-α,β-enones with N-hydroxybenzamides. The reaction proceeds through a cascade sequence of intramolecular 5-exo-dig annulation, amination, Lossen rearrangement, and decarboxylation, forming two new C-X (X = O, N) bonds in a one-step transformation. This cascade protocol features a wide substrate range and outstanding functional group compatibility and allows an efficient large-scale synthesis and downstream transformations of the target products.

accepted.title: Pd(II)-Catalyzed Decarboxylative ortho -Amidation of Benzyl Thiocyanates with Oxamic Acids Unveiling -SCN as a Bidentate Directing Group
accepted.abstract: Abstract A Pd(II)-catalyzed highly regiospecific ortho-amidation of benzyl thiocyanates with N,N-disubstituted oxamic acids has been developed using AgOAc as an oxidant. Thiocyanate (-SCN) has been introduced as a multicoordinating weak-directing group in C–H activation. The decarboxylative coupling proceeds under operationally simple conditions with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. A variety of substituted, secondary, and heterocyclic benzyl thiocyanates efficiently undergo ortho-amidation with diverse oxamic acids to afford a series of ortho-amidation products in moderate to excellent yields. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations established that the thiocyanate (-SCN) moiety acts as a bidentate directing group, coordinating to palladium through both nitrogen and sulfur atoms sequentially, thereby leading to the formation of an unusual monomeric Pd(III)-intermediate. This Pd(III)-intermediate preferentially undergoes reductive elimination to generate a Pd(I)-species rather than participating in single-electron oxidation or disproportionation pathways. The Pd(II)-catalyst is regenerated from Pd(I) using silver(I) as an oxidant. The established protocol offers an efficient and atom-economical route for C–H amidation, expanding the versatility of Pd-catalyzed C–H functionalization strategies.

accepted.title: Pd/Cu Synergistic Catalysis for Difluorocarbene-Mediated Synthesis of Carbamoyl-Substituted Oxindoles
accepted.abstract: Abstract A palladium-catalyzed tandem Heck cyclization of N-(2-iodoaryl)acrylamides with N-methylanilines and ClCF2COONa has been developed for the synthesis of carbamoyl-substituted oxindoles bearing an all-carbon quaternary stereocenter, wherein difluorocarbene serves as the carbonyl source. This method operates under mild conditions, exhibits a broad substrate scope, and features operationally simple and safe procedures. Moreover, it expands the synthetic utility of difluorocarbene-involved domino Heck cyclizations and enables the efficient construction of diverse amide-functionalized molecular architectures containing an all-carbon quaternary center.

accepted.title: Synthesis of (±)-Mersicarpine and Related Kopsia Alkaloids Frameworks via a Cyanomethyl Radical Addition/Cyclization Cascade Process
accepted.abstract: Abstract In this work, we report a concise, protecting-group-free, seven-step total synthesis of (±)-mersicarpine in 15% overall yield, from commercial γ-caprolactone, representing the shortest racemic route reported to date. In addition, formal synthetic approaches to rhazinilam and leuconoxine alkaloids were achieved. The strategy relies on a cyanomethyl radical cascade cyclization of N-alkene-linked indole and pyrrole substrates under either DLP-mediated or photoredox conditions, providing rapid access to key polycyclic frameworks.

accepted.title: Synthesis of Succinic Acids via Electrochemical Dicarboxylation of Aryl Terminal Alkynes with CO2
accepted.abstract: Abstract An environment-friendly and efficient method for the synthesis of succinic acids has been developed through the electrochemical dicarboxylation of aryl terminal alkynes with CO2. The reaction proceeds smoothly at a certain constant current in acetonitrile with manganese(II) carbonate (MnCO3) as the additive, giving the desired succinic acids with up to 85% isolated yield. The system is applicable to various aryl terminal alkynes, exhibiting good functional group tolerance. This method may open up a window for the application of the electrochemical strategy in the synthesis of multicarboxylic acids.

accepted.title: Visible-Light Photoredox Catalysis Enabled Triazole Annulation of Azidophilic Michael Acceptors
accepted.abstract: Abstract Fully substituted 1,2,3-triazoles are key functional units in modern organic chemistry owing to their diverse scientific utility. Though ene-azide cycloaddition emerged as a reliable strategy for their synthesis, it often requires metal catalysts and/or high temperature. To tackle this challenge, we herein disclose our approach of visible-light photoredox catalysis (VLPC) by employing Rose Bengal (RB) as a organo-photocatalyst. The chemistry works under blue light-emitting diode illumination by generating a solvent radical intermediate through the cooperation of RB and DMF. The reaction works well for various organic azides and Michael acceptors generating a library of substituted triazoles (50 examples) in excellent regio- and product control. The scope of the methodology is highlighted through the formal synthesis of rufinamide, an antiepileptic drug. From a technoeconomic perspective, our procedure holds sustainable advantages like room temperature, an ambient atmosphere, no byproducts, good to excellent yields, extension to gram-scale synthesis, and a safe and inexpensive catalyst.

accepted.title: Visible-Light-Driven C–H Arylation of Aminoquinones with Diaryliodonium Salts
accepted.abstract: Abstract A visible-light-driven C–H arylation of 2-amino-1,4-naphthoquinones with diaryliodonium salts has been developed using 10-phenylphenothiazine (PTH) as a photocatalyst. Mechanistic studies reveal that aminoquinone serves both as the substrate and as an electron shuttle in the electron transfer from PTH to the diaryliodonium salts. accepted.title: Insertion of Alkenes into Aryl Nitrile C–C Bonds Enabled by Thiophenolate Photocatalysis
accepted.abstract: Abstract Insertion of alkenes into chemical bonds represents a powerful strategy for carbon framework editing, yet direct insertion into C–C bonds remains a formidable challenge due to the nonpolarity, high-lying σ* orbital, steric shielding, and high thermodynamic stability of the C–C bond. Here, we present a visible-light-driven thiophenolate photocatalytic system that enables direct insertion of alkenes into the C–C bond of aryl nitriles. Mechanistic studies reveal a photoinduced single-electron transfer from the excited thiophenolate anion to the aryl nitrile, generating a radical pair that undergoes radical addition and radical–radical cross-coupling, followed by elimination and nucleophilic addition to afford the insertion product. This strategy not only provides an avenue for editing inert C–C bonds but also establishes thiophenolate photocatalysis as a platform for challenging bond constructions under transition-metal-free and redox-neutral conditions.

accepted.title: Photoenzymatic Enantioselective [2+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynes Enabled by Whole-Cell Directed Evolution
accepted.abstract: Abstract Enantioselective excited-state photocycloadditions represent an attractive yet challenging strategy for accessing optically active strained molecules. Here, we report a whole-cell directed evolution platform for engineering artificial triplet photoenzymes that catalyze the enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of alkynes. By employing calcium chloride-mediated membrane permeabilization, we overcome substrate accessibility limitations in whole-cell systems and enable high-throughput evolution without the need for cell lysates or purified enzymes. Through ten rounds of directed evolution, a primitive ancestor (APC1.0; 46% yield, 6% ee) was transformed into a highly efficient variant (APC10.0; 92% yield, 94% ee under whole-cell conditions; 99% yield, 97% ee as the purified enzyme). The enhanced activity of APC10.0 enabled a total turnover number of 1800. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the evolution of artificial photoenzymes and expands the scope of biocatalysis toward stereoselective excited-state transformations.

accepted.title: Titanium-Catalyzed Divergent Deoxycyclization for Synthesizing Semisaturated Nitrogen Heterocycles
accepted.abstract: Abstract Semisaturated nitrogen heterocycles, such as 3-pyrrolines and unsaturated azepanes, possess highly prized three-dimensional geometries for drug discovery. However, their divergent synthesis from simple, unactivated feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a highly selective, titanium-catalyzed divergent radical deoxycyclization coupling of nitrosoarenes and 1,3-dienes. Following an initial aza-Diels–Alder cycloaddition, an in situ generated low-valent titanium(III) species mediates single-electron homolytic cleavage of the robust oxazine N–O bond, yielding a transient nitrogen-centered aminyl radical. By rationally tuning the solvent coordination sphere and chlorosilane dissociation kinetics, this radical’s trajectory is selectively directed down two orthogonal pathways: a 5-exo-tet cyclization to afford 3-pyrrolines (formal [4 + 1]) and a highly strained vinylaziridine-mediated aza-Claisen rearrangement to yield unsaturated azepanes (formal [4 + 3]). This radical-polar crossover protocol features broad functional group tolerance and enables a streamlined, cyanide-free synthesis of the antiarrhythmic drug candidate SU-13197. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including EPR spin-trapping, support the crucial aminyl radical intermediacy and the important role of titanium coordination in orchestrating cascade divergence.

accepted.title: Catalytic Asymmetric 1,6-Diene Cyclization via Designed Carbocationic 5- and 6- exo Pathways
accepted.abstract: Abstract Catalytic asymmetric electrophilic alkene functionalization provides a powerful strategy for the construction of complex chiral molecules. Despite significant progress in this field, the asymmetric functionalization of alkenes promoted by an electrophilic carbon species via an exo-cyclization mode remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a solution to this challenge: alkenes can undergo designed 5-exo- and 6-exo-carbocationic cyclizations to generate optically pure, complex chiral compounds with high enantio- and diastereoselectivities. In this approach, for 1,6-dienes bearing bulky sulfonamide or quaternary carbon linkers, one double bond of the substrate interacts with an external electrophile, such as a trifluoromethylthio, arylthio, alkylthio, or chlorine species, generating an electrophilic carbon species that promotes the transformation of 1,6-dienes under chiral indane-based chalcogenide catalysis. Notably, the reaction can be terminated by intramolecular nucleophiles via cis-addition or can be captured by various intermolecular nucleophiles. A diverse array of optically pure polycyclic and monocyclic compounds can be obtained, including 5-5-6 tricyclic N-heterocycles and pentasubstituted chiral cyclohexanes. The same strategy can also be efficiently applied to 6-endo cyclizations, leading to the formation of 6-6-6 tricyclic and monocyclic N-heterocycle

accepted.title: Controlled Generation of Unstabilized N -Alkyl Nitrile Imines Enables Regioselective (3 + 2) Cycloadditions with Diverse Dipolarophiles
accepted.abstract: Abstract N-Alkyl nitrile imines remain underdeveloped as intermediates for intermolecular cycloadditions. Here, we report their in situ generation and regioselective (3 + 2) cycloaddition with activated and unactivated alkenes and alkynes, affording N-alkyl pyrazolines and pyrazoles in good to excellent yields. The method accommodates broad variation in both reaction partners and enables gram-scale preparation of a key pyrazole fragment used in the synthesis of lenacapavir in a 79% yield over two steps.

accepted.title: Criegee Intermediate-Enabled Decarboxylative C(sp3)–C(sp3) Cross-Coupling of α,β-Unsaturated Esters with Cyclic Acetals
accepted.abstract: Abstract Ozonolysis and Baeyer–Villiger (BV) rearrangement are among the earliest transformations in which cyclic/acyclic peroxo intermediates, often known as Criegee intermediates, have been detected. Herein, we disclose the merger of a Criegee intermediate with C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling via a rare anti-Giese addition for a new genre of C–C cross-coupling to access complex chemical libraries. Detailed mechanistic investigation reveals the generation of a cyclic tetrahedral peroxo intermediate (CI), and gas-phase analysis establishes the formation of 16O═C═18O under 18O2 conditions and straightforwardly supports the formation of peroxylactones via a Criegee intermediate under our standard conditions. Importantly, many pharmaceutically active drug-like molecules have been screened thoroughly and have been shown to exhibit excellent tolerance and high regioselectivity for this methodology.

accepted.title: Multidimensional Involvement of Tris(4-methoxyphenyl)amine in Electrolytic Sulfonylation of Alkenes
accepted.abstract: Abstract A tris(4-methoxyphenyl)amine (TMPA)-catalyzed paired-electrolysis sulfonylation is reported. TMPA first serves as the electron donor, thereby facilitating the reduction of sulfonyl chloride; subsequently, the resulting TMPA•+ oxidizes the benzyl radical intermediate. TMPA and the chloride anion also act as a Brønsted base to promote deprotonation at the α-carbon of the sulfonyl group. The current results elucidate a novel paradigm of triarylamine multiple activation, which may stimulate continuous exploration of multiple action modes of other mediators.

accepted.title: Pd-Catalyzed Freon-Enabled Aminocarbonylation of Aryl Iodides
accepted.abstract: Abstract A palladium-catalyzed Freon-to-carbonyl transfer strategy has been developed for the CO-free aminocarbonylation of aryl and heteroaryl iodides with amines. Using chlorodifluoromethane (Freon-22) as both a difluorocarbene precursor and a carbonyl source, this protocol enables direct access to diverse benzamide derivatives without external CO gas or conventional CO-releasing reagents. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope and good functional-group tolerance, accommodating electronically diverse aryl iodides, polycyclic and heteroaryl iodides, and primary and secondary amines. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage benzamidation of bioactive-molecule-derived substrates and concise synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant benzamide scaffolds, including trimethobenzamide and methyl tamibarotene. Mechanistic experiments involving benzimidazole trapping and H218O labeling support a difluorocarbene-derived carbonyl-transfer process in which water contributes to the oxygen atom of the amide carbonyl group. This work establishes Freon-22 as a practical carbonyl surrogate for CO-free amide synthesis.

accepted.abstract: Abstract A method for skeletal editing of C–C σ-bonds in strained alicycles via single-carbon insertion is reported. This skeletal editing method for cyclobutanols differs from well-established semipinacol rearrangement pathways, offering an efficient route to cyclopentanols by direct scaffold hopping of cyclobutanols. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions in good yields, expanding the toolkit for single-atom insertion into C–C σ-bonds.

accepted.title: Scaffold Hopping of Pyrimidines into 2-Acylpyrroles
accepted.abstract: Abstract A practical skeletal-editing strategy was developed for the conversion of 4-substituted pyrimidines into 2-acyl-5-arylpyrroles. The transformation directly converts a six-membered, electron-deficient pyrimidine into a five-membered azole while simultaneously installing an acyl group. The reaction sequence involves pyrimidine activation, ring-opening, fragmentation, and ring reconstruction. Central to this strategy is the controlled generation of pyrimidine-derived vinamidinium salts as open-chain A4 synthons, which are then intercepted by α-bromoketones as functionalized annulation reagents. The developed scaffold-hopping method can be applied for late-stage modification of pyrimidine-containing bioactive or pharmaceutical molecules.

accepted.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis of Enteropeptin A Analogues
accepted.abstract: Abstract Enteropeptin A is a sactipeptide natural product featuring a unique six-membered thiomorpholine core. Herein, we describe a solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)-compatible approach to enteropeptin A analogues featuring a simplified sactionine motif. The strategy employs a readily accessible building block and efficient on-resin assembly. A “N to C” variant, differing in the directionality of the sactionine linkage was also readily accessible. Collectively, this work accelerates access to analogues of this important class of natural products.

accepted.title: Stereoselective Synthesis of Linustedastat Via Deoxy-Aromatization Strategy
accepted.abstract: Abstract An efficient and stereoselective synthesis of Linustedastat (1) is reported, commencing from inexpensive and commercially available sitolactone. The route features a highly chemoselective Grignard addition, followed by sequential double aldol condensations to construct the core steroidal framework. A key step involves a novel deoxy-aromatization of a fluorinated steroid intermediate, setting the stage for a stereoselective hydrogenation and a 1,4-conjugate addition to further elaborate the molecule. This strategically designed sequence delivers the complex and electron-deficient fluorinated steroidal architecture in 16 steps with an 11.0% overall yield.

accepted.title: Synthesis of α-Cyano-β-naphthylamines via Tandem Selective Hydrocyanation of Unactivated Alkynes and Thorpe Reaction
accepted.abstract: Abstract An unprecedented nickel-catalyzed tandem reaction involving alkyne hydrocyanation and sequential Thorpe reaction has been developed. By employing readily available and less toxic Zn(CN)2 as the cyanide source, both selective alkyne hydrocyanation and tandem cyclization are achieved in a substrate-controlled manner. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations confirm that the alkenyl nitrile serves as a key intermediate, and hydrogen transfer is identified as the rate-determining step in the Thorpe reaction. This work offers a novel strategy for the construction of α-cyano-β-naphthylamine via a cascade reaction mode.

accepted.title: Synthesis of Pyrido[2,3- d ]pyrimidin-4(3 H )-ones via SNAr/Tandem Cyclization
accepted.abstract: Abstract A new method has been developed for constructing the pyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidin-4(3H)-one scaffold under metal- and ligand-free conditions. In this strategy, 2-bromo-N-phenylnicotinamide is activated by the synergistic electron-withdrawing effects of the pyridine ring and the amide group, enabling tandem nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr)/cyclization with cyanamide or formamide under simple conditions. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support an SNAr/cyclization mechanism. Preliminary photophysical studies show that the products exhibit blue emission, suggesting potential applications in materials science. Additionally, molecular docking studies indicate that the synthesized scaffold may have relevance to medicinal chemistry, providing a foundation for future biological evaluations.

rejected.title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
rejected.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

rejected.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
rejected.abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. rejected.title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
rejected.abstract: Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. rejected.title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
rejected.abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

rejected.title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
rejected.abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

rejected.title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
rejected.abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

rejected.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer

rejected.title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
rejected.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. rejected.title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
rejected.abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

rejected.title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
rejected.abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. rejected.title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
rejected.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children. rejected.abstract: Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ L to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

rejected.title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
rejected.abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and • OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film • OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase • OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

rejected.abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. rejected.title: Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH 4 hydroxylation
rejected.abstract: Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu 1 to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO 2 , -H, and -CH 3 ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu 1 sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu 1 sites, thereby facilitating CH 4 activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO 2 -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu 1 - • OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu 1 /U6-NO 2 achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h −1 with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

rejected.title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
rejected.abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

rejected.title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
rejected.abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000–2009 to 1.7 days in 2010–2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

rejected.title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
rejected.abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

rejected.title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
rejected.abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

rejected.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
rejected.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

rejected.title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
rejected.abstract: Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m −2 ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m −2 from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

rejected.title: The network structure of the urban revolution
rejected.abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

rejected.title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
rejected.abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. rejected.title: Multicomponent Nanocrystal Superlattice Structure Prediction from First-Principles Validated against Two Decades of Experiments
rejected.abstract: Abstract Predicting nanocrystal (nanoparticle) assembly into ordered arrays (superlattices) is a grand challenge in materials chemistry that has largely resisted first-principles theories. Here, we extend MOLT-CF, a classical density functional theory, to multicomponent nanocrystal systems and subject it to a rigorous validation by comparing against nearly 300 experiments spanning two decades of literature. We use MOLT-CF to predict stability and phase diagrams for binary superlattices of nanocrystals with linear hydrocarbon ligands, as well as many other fine structural details, for example, lattice constants, packing fractions, ligand structure, and, in the case of (cubic) perovskite nanocrystals, orientation. Significant discrepancies from experiments are noted only for the Li3Bi and Cu3Au superlattices. In the former, we predict that this lattice is stabilized by particle fractionalization, which is supported by a reexamination of experimental data in the literature. In the case of Cu3Au (for which MOLT-CF predicts thermodynamic instability against phase separation into single-component lattices), we propose two alternative candidate structures that reconcile theory with experimental observations. These results establish MOLT-CF as a rigorous platform for the computational design of next-generation functional nanoparticle materials.

rejected.title: On-Surface Synthesis of a Low Bandgap Cyclopenta[ c , d ]azulene-Based Polymer
rejected.abstract: Abstract Nonbenzenoid topologies offer a compelling strategy to tailor the electronic properties of low-dimensional carbon materials. Here, we report the on-surface synthesis of a nonalternant polymer incorporating a [7–5–5] cyclopenta[c,d]azulene (CPA) motif on Au(111) via thermally induced Ullmann coupling. Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy confirms the robustness of the [7–5–5] framework. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy, together with dI/dV mapping supported by density functional theory calculations, reveals a remarkable narrow polymeric bandgap of 1.5 eV. The electronic structure is governed by the intramolecular charge transfer from the heptagonal ring to the adjacent fused pentagonal rings, resulting in a pronounced dipole moment despite being composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen. Aromaticity analyses indicate the coexistence of locally aromatic and slightly antiaromatic regions, highlighting the intrinsic electronic frustration associated with the nonalternant topology. These findings demonstrate how the controlled incorporation of [7–5–5] motifs enables the rational bandgap engineering in carbon-based polymers and expands the scope of nonbenzenoid design in on-surface synthesis.

rejected.abstract: Abstract We present a systematic study of noble metal (Pt, Pd, Ir, and Rh) single-atom cocatalysts decorated on p-type and quantum-confined TiO2 nanotubes for photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia. All single-atom cocatalysts were prepared through a reactive deposition using different metal precursors, resulting in a single-atom oxidation state (δ+) of δ ≈ 2. At a similar loading concentration (0.2–0.3 at%) and in the absence of any sacrificial agent, Pd single atoms exhibit the highest element-specific activity for ammonia production, while Pt single atoms display a prominent photocatalytic activity with a strong tendency of nitrite reduction toward ammonia. Rh single atoms achieve the highest ammonia selectivity, whereas Ir single atoms predominantly produce nitrite due to inhibited subsequent reduction. Comparisons with single atoms deposited on conventional TiO2 (P25) and with nanoparticles supported on the nanotubes reveal that both the semiconductor properties (quantum confinement effect and p-type conductivity) and the speciation of the cocatalyst (single atom) can significantly enhance activity and selectivity. These findings aid in establishing design principles for different single-atom catalysts toward efficient and selective photocatalytic nitrogen valorization.

rejected.title: The Molecular Logic of Platelet-Activating Factor (PAF)
rejected.abstract: Abstract Platelet-activating factor (PAF) is a well-known if enigmatic lipid signal with important roles in inflammatory responses, allergic reactions, autoimmune diseases, and thrombotic cascades. Several lines of evidence suggest that our current model of PAF’s molecular mechanism is inadequate. This report describes a recontextualized model for PAF. The revised model embeds PAF in a plasmalogen-based molecular mechanism in which activation is a spontaneous chemical reaction triggered by environmental conditions that liberates a PAF receptor (PAF-R) agonist from a membrane-bound phospholipid. The active ligand subsequently undergoes a thermodynamically driven spontaneous rearrangement into an inactive isomer, a feature that controls response lifetime. The revised model is a molecule-autonomous set of transformations that create a response with spatial and temporal control. More generally the revised model’s congruence with a similar model for RORγt supports a picture in which plasmalogens form a part of the immune system that is separate from the cell-based innate and adaptive immune systems.

rejected.abstract: Abstract Using porous adsorbents to achieve efficient capture of radioactive iodine from nuclear waste under industrial conditions remains a formidable challenge, since most adsorbents just exhibit a low iodine uptake under such conditions. The two COFs feature a minimal-transitivity [3 4] flu-derived net, which allows anisotropic isoreticular expansion through a general sequential derived-net approach. ECUT-COF-100 was found to give an ultrahigh iodine uptake of 1.51 g/g under simulated industrial conditions (150 °C and 150 ppmv I2), 5.2-fold that of ECUT-COF-99 (0.29 g/g). Such performance also far exceeds all established organic adsorbents for this use. Mechanism studies reveal that nonaromatic tertiary nitrogen atoms allow for strong charge transfer from the lone-pair electrons of tertiary nitrogen to I2, leading to the formation of ionic iodides (I3– and I5–) and the N·+ radical cation and then fixing of ionic iodides by Coulomb interactions. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent with record iodine uptake for radioactive iodine capture from nuclear waste but also highlights a new insight into the tertiary nitrogen effect in 3D COFs for efficient iodine capture.

rejected.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

rejected.title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
rejected.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models.

rejected.title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development
rejected.abstract: Abstract Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

rejected.title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
rejected.abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.

We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

rejected.title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
rejected.abstract: Abstract Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.

rejected.title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
rejected.abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na 2 O/Na 2 CO 3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10 −7 S cm −1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na 2 O (10 −12 S cm −1 ) and Na 2 CO 3 (10 −23 S cm −1 ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g ‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

Here, we show that this apparent quiescence is accompanied by a heightened vulnerability to electron transport chain (ETC)‐associated perturbation by guanidinium‐based cationic polymers. PO 3 G, a representative polymer, preferentially kills persister‐enriched populations while markedly perturbing respiratory electron transfer. Following this ETC‐associated perturbation, persister‐enriched populations exhibit sustained superoxide‐associated oxidative stress and fail to restore NADH/NAD + homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of viability. Consistent with this ETC dependency, PO 3 G also markedly reduces persister‐enriched population induced by diverse triggers across bacterial species and achieves up to 7‐log reductions in bacterial burden in vivo. These results establish a mechanistic link between cationic polymer‐induced ETC‐associated perturbation and persister elimination, highlighting limited recovery from respiratory and redox perturbation as a vulnerability underlying the preferential killing of persisters.

rejected.title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
rejected.abstract: Abstract Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

rejected.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
rejected.abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea.
